title: Congruence
content: **Congruence** is a structure with a residue $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, a modulus $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n > 0$. It represents the residue class $\{x \in \mathbb{Z} : x \equiv a \pmod{n}\}$.
mathContext: A congruence class $a \pmod{n}$ contains exactly $1/n$ of all integers. The density of covered integers by a system of congruences with distinct moduli $n_1, \ldots, n_k$ can be computed using inclusion-exclusion.

title: Satisfies Congruence
content: **Congruence.satisfies c x** holds when $x \equiv c.\mathrm{residue} \pmod{c.\mathrm{modulus}}$. Uses Mathlib's `Int.ModEq`.
mathContext: $x \equiv a \pmod{n}$ means $n \mid (x - a)$. This is the fundamental relation in covering system theory.

title: Congruence System
content: **CongruenceSystem** is a finite set of congruences with **distinct moduli**. The distinct-moduli condition is standard in covering system theory.
mathContext: A covering system is a collection $\{a_i \pmod{n_i}\}_{i=1}^k$ with $n_1 < \ldots < n_k$ such that every integer belongs to at least one class. The distinct-moduli requirement is part of the classical definition.

title: Covered Integer
content: **CongruenceSystem.covers S x** holds if $x$ satisfies at least one congruence in $S$.
mathContext: $S.\mathrm{covers}(x) \;\Leftrightarrow\; \exists c \in S,\; x \equiv c.a \pmod{c.n}$. By inclusion-exclusion, the covering density involves LCMs of moduli subsets.

title: Uncovered Integer
content: **CongruenceSystem.uncovered S x** holds if $x$ satisfies no congruence in $S$. The density of uncovered integers is what Erdős asked about.
mathContext: $S.\mathrm{uncovered}(x) \;\Leftrightarrow\; \forall c \in S,\; x \not\equiv c.a \pmod{c.n}$. For a perfect covering, there are no uncovered integers.

title: Uncovered Density
content: **uncoveredDensity S M** is the fraction of integers in $[1, M]$ uncovered by $S$.
mathContext: $\delta_M(S) = |\{m \in [1,M] : S.\mathrm{uncovered}(m)\}|/M$. By the Chinese Remainder Theorem, this stabilizes for $M \geq \mathrm{lcm}(n_1, \ldots, n_k)$.

title: Asymptotic Uncovered Density
content: **asymptoticUncoveredDensity S** is $\liminf_{M \to \infty} \delta_M(S)$. Using liminf ensures well-definedness.
mathContext: $\delta(S) = \liminf_{M \to \infty} \delta_M(S)$. For finite systems, the limit exists and equals $|\{m \in [1,L] : S.\mathrm{uncovered}(m)\}|/L$ where $L = \mathrm{lcm}$ of all moduli.

title: ε-Almost Covering
content: **IsAlmostCovering S ε** asserts $\delta(S) \leq \varepsilon$. Can we achieve arbitrarily small $\varepsilon$ with moduli in $[N, CN]$ for fixed $C$?
mathContext: $\mathrm{IsAlmostCovering}(S, \varepsilon) \;\Leftrightarrow\; \liminf_{M \to \infty} \delta_M(S) \leq \varepsilon$. For moduli in $[N, CN]$, the averaging argument gives $\delta(S) \geq \prod_{n=N}^{CN}(1-1/n) \approx 1/C$.

title: Perfect Covering
content: **IsPerfectCovering S** means every integer is covered ($\varepsilon = 0$). Erdős (1950) showed these exist with all moduli $> 1$; the minimum modulus question was resolved by BBMST.

title: Moduli in Range
content: **HasModuliInRange S N M** requires all moduli in $[N, M]$. The bounded-range constraint makes the problem nontrivial.
mathContext: For moduli in $[N, CN]$, the total coverage is $\sum_{n=N}^{CN} 1/n \approx \ln C$, bounded for fixed $C$. This is why constant $C$ fails: finite total coverage cannot make uncovered density arbitrarily small.

title: Natural Density Product
content: **naturalDensity m₁ m₂** = $\prod_{n=m_1}^{m_2}(1-1/n)$. This is the best achievable uncovered density by the averaging (random residue) argument.
mathContext: $\prod_{n=N}^{CN}(1-1/n) = \frac{(N-1)!/(CN)!}{\text{(scaling)}} \approx \frac{N-1}{CN} \approx 1/C$. For fixed $C$, this is bounded below by $1/C > 0$, proving that the uncovered density cannot vanish.

title: Erdős Conjecture ($100 Prize)
content: **ErdosConjecture**: $\exists C > 1$ such that $\forall \varepsilon > 0,\; \forall N \geq 1$, an $\varepsilon$-almost covering with moduli in $[N, CN]$ exists. Answer: NO.
mathContext: The conjecture asks for a universal constant $C$. FFKPY showed no such $C$ exists: for any fixed $C > 1$, the uncovered density is bounded below by $\approx 1/(2C)$ for large $N$.

title: Conjecture Negation
content: **ErdosConjectureNegation**: $\forall C > 1,\; \exists \varepsilon > 0,\; \exists N$ such that no system with moduli in $[N, CN]$ achieves $\varepsilon$-almost covering. This is what was PROVED.
mathContext: The negation swaps quantifiers: $\forall C > 1,\; \exists \varepsilon > 0,\; \exists N$ such that every system $S$ with moduli in $[N, CN]$ has $\delta(S) > \varepsilon$.

title: Critical Exponent
content: **criticalExponent N** = $\frac{\log\log\log N}{4\log\log N}$. For $C \leq N^{\alpha(N)}$, almost-covering provably fails.
mathContext: $\alpha(N) = \frac{\log\log\log N}{4\log\log N} \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$, but extremely slowly. For $N = 10^{100}$, $\alpha(N) \approx 0.045$, so $N^{\alpha(N)} \approx 10^{4.5}$.

title: FFKPY Main Theorem
content: **ffkpy_main_theorem**: For large $N$, if $1 < C \leq N^{\alpha(N)}$, every system with moduli in $[N, CN]$ has $\delta(S) \geq \frac{1}{2}\prod_c(1-1/c.n)$.
mathContext: Since $\prod_{n=N}^{CN}(1-1/n) \geq 1/C$, this gives $\delta(S) \geq 1/(2C) > 0$ for fixed $C$, proving the conjecture false.

title: Conjecture Disproved
content: **erdos_27_disproved**: `ErdosConjectureNegation` holds. No constant $C > 1$ works. This resolved Erdős's $\$100$ prize.
mathContext: For any $C > 1$, choose $N$ large enough that $C \leq N^{\alpha(N)}$, then $\delta(S) \geq 1/(2C)$ for all $S$. Setting $\varepsilon = 1/(4C)$ refutes the conjecture.

title: Growing C Works
content: **growing_C_works**: If $C = C(N)$ grows with $N$, $\varepsilon$-almost coverings exist for any fixed $\varepsilon$.
mathContext: For $C(N) \to \infty$, $\prod_{n=N}^{C(N)N}(1-1/n) \to 0$, so the averaging argument gives uncovered density $\to 0$.

title: Sufficient C
content: **sufficientC N** = $N^{1/\log\log N}$. This is sufficient for almost-covering and grows faster than the critical exponent threshold.
mathContext: $C(N) = N^{1/\log\log N}$ satisfies $\log C(N) = \log N/\log\log N \to \infty$, so $C(N) \to \infty$. Since $1/\log\log N \gg \alpha(N)$, this exceeds the critical threshold.

title: BBMST Bound
content: **bbmst_bound**: Every perfect covering has some modulus $< 616{,}000$ (Bloom-Briggs-Maynard-Smith-Tao 2024). Resolves the Erdős minimum modulus conjecture.
mathContext: Hough (2015) first proved the conjecture with bound $10^{18}$. Balister et al. improved to $10^6$. BBMST achieved $616{,}000$. This means no covering system can have all moduli $\geq 616{,}000$.
